cohort: The study enrolled 685 patients with endometriosis-associated infertility from January 2018 to December 2020, divided into CE (318) and non-CE (367) groups, with a subset of 123 clinically pregnant women from the CE group and 369 from the non-CE group selected for detailed comparison.
finding: Chronic endometritis (CE) is prevalent among patients with endometriosis-associated infertility and is linked to increased risks of pregnancy complications, including placenta previa, gestational hypertension, and cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Patients with chronic endometritis had increased risks of cesarean sections (59.34%).
